title: Achilles Tendinitis
claims: AAOS distinguishes noninsertional Achilles tendinitis, which more commonly affects younger active people especially runners, from insertional tendinitis at the heel attachment, which often involves calf tightness and bone spurs.
AAOS warns that a sudden pop in the back of the calf or heel may indicate a torn Achilles tendon and requires immediate medical assessment.
AAOS states cortisone injections into the Achilles tendon are not recommended because they can cause tendon rupture, with research showing decreased tendon strength.
AAOS says heel-drop eccentric exercises are for noninsertional tendinitis only and should not be performed with insertional tendinitis.
AAOS notes even with early treatment pain may last longer than 3 months, and surgery is considered only after 6 months of nonsurgical treatment.
AAOS advises not using NSAIDs for more than 1 month without talking to a primary care doctor.
